questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Pick up or drop off passengers here.
Do not park, stand, or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not park, stand, or stop.
questions.explanation: A red curb means you cannot stop, stand, or park there.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road

questions.explanation: Speeding, not paying attention, and following too closely are all major causes of accidents. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too close.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of the road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Do not pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Pass when safe.
Traffic moves the same direction. Do not pass.
Traffic moves the same direction. Pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Do not pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Which must you obey over the others?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beams so other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you reduce hydroplaning risk?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on water instead of gripping the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when following another vehicle. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes will soon merge into one lane.

questions.question: What are the requirements for driving on an interstate?

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly during a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once you are moving slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must you account for?

options.text: Trucks need more distance to stop.
Trucks need less distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you and where you can see traffic clearly.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is speeding above the legal limit.

questions.question: In New York, what blood alcohol content (BAC) level shows intoxication?
questions.explanation: In New York, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is proof of intoxication. A BAC of 0.05 percent or higher shows impairment.

questions.question: Which action blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Using public transportation instead of a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams. Avoid this behavior.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to police?

options.text: After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
Only when stopped for a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: After a crash or when stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance when driving. Show it to a police officer after a crash or traffic stop upon request.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked spot at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can speed up to match traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can speed up to match traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a large enough gap to speed up to the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You can turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. You must yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.
